subject: Clarify per-token metrics, streaming rounding, and discount caps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liz Moran <liz.moran@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:02:00Z
Subject: Clarify per-token metrics, streaming rounding, and discount caps

Liz / Procurement team —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our pricing discussion I wanted to summarize Redwood's proposed commit tiers and surface a few specific metric definitions we need to align on before legal drafts the amendment. Goal: get language in the SOW so we can turn on the committed discount structure without surprises during PoC.

Summary of commercial proposal (high level):
- 3-tier commit: 0-1M tokens/month (list price), 1M-10M tokens/month (10% committed discount), >10M tokens/month (18% committed discount)
- Monthly true-up with 60-day invoice window
- Streaming usage billed at per-output-token rate (same unit price as completion tokens)

Open metric questions we need confirmed from Acme:
1) "Billable tokens" definition: Are we aligned that billable tokens = total tokens consumed for request + response as counted by the tokenizer used by the serving runtime (BPE/byte-pair encoding), not characters? This impacts cost materially for your short-turnaround chat flows.
2) Streaming rounding for live UX: Redwood normally bills streaming output at token granularity and charges for every emitted token; for streaming with chunked delivery we internally buffer and emit partial tokens rarely — how does Acme prefer rounding to be expressed in the contract? Typical options: round up to nearest token (default), or aggregate per-second and round to nearest token-per-second for high-frequency low-token flows.
3) Rounding / microbilling floor: For sub-token timing (e.g., keepalive heartbeats or empty-ack frames), we can add an explicit carve-out so non-content frames are not billed.
4) Carryover & caps: commit carryforward allowed up to 25% of unused committed units for the following quarter? Or would Acme prefer monthly carryforward only?

Requested next step: please reply with the preferred answers to 1–4, and we will attach a redline with explicit clause language. I attached Redwood_Metric_Definitions_v2.pdf and the current commit summary for reference.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: Redwood_Metric_Definitions_v2.pdf, Acme_Commit_Summary.xlsx
From: Liz Moran <liz.moran@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify per-token metrics, streaming rounding, and discount caps

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick points from Acme:
- On (1) we prefer an explicit tokenizer spec in the contract ("billable tokens measured using the GPT-style BPE tokenizer as implemented in the runtime at the time of billing"). That way we avoid character-vs-token ambiguity.
- On (2) our product team is worried about microbilling for streaming chat (we have many sub-second token bursts). We would rather have a per-streaming-session aggregation: bill by total emitted tokens per session and round up to the nearest whole token (so no per-100ms billing). Alternatively, if Redwood insists on streaming-by-chunk, we need a monthly cap on streaming microcharges (e.g., no more than 3% of monthly bill can be from rounding artifacts).
- On (3) yes please carve out keep-alives and health-check frames from billable units.
- On (4) Acme prefers monthly carryforward only (no multi-month carryover) and a true-up at month-end; we need a 30-day notice before applying any carryforward credits to prevent surprise usage patterns.

I looped in Girish (procurement) for procurement/legal follow-up. Can you propose specific clause language we can take to our counsel?

Best,
Liz Moran
Director, Platform Partnerships | Acme Enterprises
liz.moran@acme.com

---
Forwarded to: Girish Patel <girish.patel@acme.com>
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify per-token metrics, streaming rounding, and discount caps (internal)

Karthik / Aditya —

Draft language proposal below that balances Acme's asks and Redwood's billing model. I recommend we offer the tokenizer spec + a pragmatic streaming rounding clause with a monthly rounding artifact cap (Liz suggested 3%, we could counter at 2%). Also propose limiting the carryforward to one month (aligns with Acme).

Proposed contract snippets (for legal to insert into SOW/Amendment):

1) Billable Units: "Billable tokens" means the number of input and output tokens as determined by the UTF-8 byte-based BPE tokenizer implemented by Redwood's serving runtime at the time of request. Changes to the tokenizer implementation that materially alter token counts will be communicated 60 days in advance and Redwood will provide a per-customer migration report.

2) Streaming Rounding: For streaming responses, Customer will be billed for actual emitted tokens. To avoid microbilling for high-frequency streams, Redwood will aggregate emitted tokens per streaming session and charge for the total emitted tokens rounded up to the nearest whole token. For sessions where partial-token emission cannot be fully attributed to content (e.g., heartbeat frames), such frames will be excluded from billable units.

3) Rounding Artifacts Cap: Notwithstanding the foregoing, rounding artifacts resulting solely from streaming chunking and session-based aggregation will not exceed 2% of Customer's monthly billed usage; any rounding artifact in excess of that amount will be credited to Customer on the next invoice.

4) Carryforward: Unused committed units may be carried forward for one subsequent monthly billing period only, up to 100% of the unused monthly commit. Unused units beyond that window expire. Application of carryforward credits requires 30 days' notice prior to application.

If Aditya/legal think these are reasonable, I'll add them into the proposed_amendment_11b.docx and send to Acme with a short note. If we think 2% is too generous, we can counter at 1.5% — but I think 2% is a good compromise.

-Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Liz Moran <liz.moran@acme.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarify per-token metrics, streaming rounding, and discount caps

Liz / Girish —

Thanks for the quick feedback and for surfacing procurement preferences. Per our internal alignment (see Marissa's draft language below), please find attached a redline that implements the tokenizer spec, streaming aggregation, exclusion of heartbeat frames, a 2% monthly rounding-artifact cap, and one-month carryforward. Key points:

- Tokenizer: we will specify the BPE tokenizer and commit to 60-day notice for material tokenizer changes and provide a migration report.
- Streaming: bill by total emitted tokens per streaming session rounded up to the nearest whole token; non-content frames excluded.
- Rounding cap: Redwood proposes 2% monthly cap on rounding artifacts (credit mechanism on next invoice).
- Carryforward: up to 100% of unused monthly commit carried forward for one month; application requires 30-day notice.

Please review the attached proposed_amendment_11b.docx and confirm whether Acme legal wants the 2% cap reduced to 1.5% or whether we should proceed with legal redlines on our side. If acceptable, I'll have our legal team circulate the formal amendment for signature. Can we aim to have this wrapped by 2026-12-06 to coincide with your internal procurement window?

Next actions:
- Acme: confirm accept/reject of 2% cap and one-month carryforward by 2026-12-03
- Redwood: if accepted, legal will prepare final amendment and share for countersign

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_amendment_11b.docx (redline), Redwood_Metric_Definitions_v2.pdf, Acme_Commit_Summary.xlsx
